Hi Sarah / Aaron —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Recap from discovery
- Primary goal: evaluate inference economics and SLA tradeoffs for ACME’s customer-facing chat assistant (English, median prompt ~120 tokens).
- Key success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms at target concurrency, cost per 1M tokens <$X (TBD), model quality parity with current hyperscaler baseline on our prompt set.
- Non-functional: KMS integration (FIPS/HSM) and audit logs for compliance.

Proposed bake-off scope (high-level)
1) Latency/throughput: Redwood hosted + Dedicated config vs Hyperscaler-managed endpoints (baseline) — measure p50/p95/p99 across small/medium/large prompts and batching.
2) Cost analysis: synthetic and production-style runs to estimate per-token unit cost at 100k and 1M token volumes.
3) Quality/regression: run ACME prompt set (sample attached) and evaluate top-1 correctness / hallucination rate / safety flags.
4) Failure modes & fallbacks: simulate node loss and degraded capacity to validate fallback behavior.

Owners & timeline (proposed)
- Redwood SE lead: Aditya Rao — test config + run scripts + result bundle (owner).
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole — kickoff, commercial questions, pricing/reporting.
- Redwood Sales Eng mgr: Vanessa Ortiz — capacity/priority and any Dedicated booking questions.
- ACME counterparts: Sarah Jenkins (PM), Aaron Li (Infra).

Timeline
- Kickoff/test design review: Mon 2026-06-29 (30 min)
- Test window: 2026-07-01 -> 2026-07-07
- Results + recommendations: by 2026-07-09

I attached a draft test plan (ACME_bakeoff_test_plan.xlsx) and a sample prompt file to get started. Please confirm the timeline and any additional success criteria you want us to prioritize.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications/priorities from our side:

Priority tests
- 1) Latency p95 at target concurrency (we’re most sensitive here). Please prioritize a test that mimics 1k concurrent users with realistic think times.
- 2) Throughput/cost at batch sizes we typically use (batch=1 and batch=8).
- 3) Quality/regression on our 150 prompt sample. We’ll mark prompts by category (completion, extraction, multi-turn).

Success thresholds (ACME provisional)
- p95 < 350ms for single-token generation for L2 users, p99 < 600ms.
- Quality delta vs baseline: <5% drop in top-1 correctness on core prompt set.

We’ll send the annotated prompt set and ground truth labels by EOD today (attached). Also, we do want the KMS/HSM integration notes early — is that something you can provide during the kickoff?

Agree on the kickoff Monday — 10am PT works for us.

—Sarah

Thanks Marissa — confirmed. Quick tech notes and actions I’ll own: 

Planned test config
- Models: Redwood-curated opt-1 (quantized) and a comparable hyperscaler model endpoint (customer provided baseline).
- Sequence lengths: {short: 32, medium: 128, long: 384} to cover ACME profiles.
- Concurrency profile: 1k simulated users using our load harness with poisson think times (modeling production).
- Batch sizes: 1 and 8.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1M tokens, memory/KV-cache hit rates, CPU/GPU utilization.

Deliverables & timeline
- Test harness + runbook: 2026-06-30 EOD (will post to drive).
- Test execution window: 2026-07-01 -> 2026-07-07 (will run multiple iterations across different Dedicated configs).
- Initial results snapshot: 2026-07-03 (smoke results).
- Final results + artifacts: 2026-07-09.

Infra ask: Rishi — can you grant a dedicated test pool for 72 hours within that window (preferred: 07/02-07/04) so we can run sustained concurrency without noisy neighbors? If not possible, we’ll coordinate burst windows on hosted lanes.

Notes on comparators: we’ll capture model-size parity and equivalent serving configs (quantization, kernels) to ensure apples-to-apples. Also logging hooks for audit events will be enabled to capture KMS/HSM usage notes for ACME’s security team.

I’ll post the run harness link and preliminary runbook to the shared Drive by EOD tomorrow.

—Aditya
